gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, at XGIMI's US store on 2026-11-14, the $479 MoGo 4 is the only one of ChatGPT's five picks whose battery is rated for a full film (2.5 h): the $249 Vibe One is rated for 1.2 h of video (RTINGS measured 103 min), the $399 Elfin Flip Plus and the $359 MoGo 2 Pro have no battery, and the 5-hour MoGo 4 + PowerBase Stand bundle costs $519, which is over the $500 cap.
standout_why: Pages compared: RTINGS 'Best Projectors Under $500' (updated 2026-11-03) has no prices, lumen figures or battery numbers. Its picks are the Epson CO-FH02, NexiGo PJ40 Pro, Wanbo X5 Pro, XGIMI Vibe One and Nebula P1i, and the MoGo 4 is only a notable mention. RTINGS 'Best Portable' (updated 2026-10-16) gives the Vibe One's measured 103 min, but its other picks (Elfin Flip 4K, Flip Laser, Mars 3) are all over $500, and it shows no prices. The Hook Up gives a measured 484 lm and 90 min on a power bank for the Elfin Flip Plus at $379, but it does not cover the MoGo 4, Vibe One or MoGo 2 Pro. ProjectorVerdict covers none of ChatGPT's five cards except the MoGo 2 Pro, at about $599. None of these pages lines up today's store prices against battery runtime, and none notes that the 5-hour MoGo 4 bundle goes over $500.
decides: If the shopper wants a battery, this confirms the MoGo 4 at $479 and rules out the Vibe One for a whole movie. The Vibe One is rated for 1.2 h, and RTINGS measured 103 min, which is shorter than many feature films. A shopper who needs more than 2.5 h has to go over budget ($519 bundle) or carry a power bank. If the projector will stay plugged in, the Elfin Flip Plus at $399 stays the value pick. The plain Elfin Flip at $303 (400 ISO lumens claimed) is a cheaper way into the same body that ChatGPT did not show.
